title: Arrival in Sidom
summary: Alma and Amulek depart the city and come to the land of Sidom. There they find people who had departed Ammonihah. An account is related concerning wives and children, those relating it, and their deliverance.

explicit_facts.text: Alma and Amulek were commanded to depart the city; they departed and came to the land of Sidom.
In Sidom they found the people who had departed Ammonihah, who had been cast out and stoned because they believed Alma's words.
An account was related concerning wives and children, those relating it, and their power of deliverance.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma and Amulek meet the people in Sidom.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of Sidom and the travel route.
The number and appearance of the people.

narration.text: Alma and Amulek were commanded to depart out of that city; and they departed, and came out even into the land of Sidom;
And they related unto them all that had happened unto their wives and children, and also concerning themselves, and of their power of deliverance.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Verse 2 reports an account but does not give its spoken words.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the earlier casting out or stoning as occurring during this meeting.
Do not invent what happened to the wives and children or supply dialogue for the account.

title: Zeezrom Hears Alma and Amulek Are in Sidom
summary: Zeezrom lies sick at Sidom with a burning fever caused by tribulations of his mind over his wickedness. He supposes Alma and Amulek have been slain because of his iniquity. When he hears they are in Sidom, he takes courage and sends a message asking them to come to him.

explicit_facts.text: Zeezrom lay sick at Sidom with a burning fever caused by great tribulations of his mind on account of his wickedness.
Zeezrom supposed Alma and Amulek had been slain because of his iniquity.
When Zeezrom heard Alma and Amulek were in the land of Sidom, he took courage and sent a message desiring them to come to him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Zeezrom can be shown lying ill.
unspecified_visual_details: Zeezrom's surroundings.
How Zeezrom hears the news and sends the message.

narration.text: Zeezrom lay sick at Sidom, with a burning fever,
which was caused by the great tribulations of his mind on account of his wickedness,
he supposed that they had been slain because of his iniquity.
his heart began to take courage; and he sent a message immediately unto them, desiring them to come unto him.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Zeezrom's belief that Alma and Amulek had been slain is not confirmation that they were.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Alma and Amulek as slain or physically present with Zeezrom.
Do not invent a messenger's identity or speech, or a visible supernatural cause for the fever.

title: Zeezrom Asks to Be Healed
summary: Alma and Amulek went immediately in response to the message and entered Zeezrom's house. They found him on his bed, very ill with a burning fever and distressed because of his iniquities. When he saw them, he stretched out his hand and asked them to heal him.

explicit_facts.text: Alma and Amulek went immediately in response to the message and entered Zeezrom's house.
They found Zeezrom on his bed, very ill with a burning fever; his mind was exceedingly sore because of his iniquities.
When Zeezrom saw them, he stretched out his hand and asked them to heal him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Zeezrom reaches toward Alma and Amulek from his bed.
unspecified_visual_details: The characters' appearances.
The house's appearance and furnishings.

narration.text: And it came to pass that they went immediately, obeying the message which he had sent unto them;
and they found him upon his bed, sick, being very low with a burning fever;
and when he saw them he stretched forth his hand, and besought them that they would heal him.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Alma and Amulek are identified as the visitors by the supplied preceding-scene context, not named in this verse. Zeezrom's mental distress is attributed to his iniquities; it is not itself a visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent words for Zeezrom's reported request or depict a healing.
Do not invent the characters' appearances or the house's furnishings.

summary: Alma takes Zeezrom by the hand and asks whether he believes in Christ's power unto salvation. Zeezrom says he believes Alma's teachings.

explicit_facts.text: Alma took Zeezrom by the hand and asked if he believed in Christ's power unto salvation.
Zeezrom answered that he believed all the words Alma had taught.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma holds Zeezrom's hand as they speak.

title: Zeezrom Affirms His Belief
summary: Alma tells Zeezrom he can be healed if he believes in Christ's redemption. Zeezrom answers that he believes according to Alma's words.

summary: The people in Ammonihah remain hard-hearted and do not repent. They attribute Alma and Amulek's power to the devil and do not believe in repentance.
